Moburst | Company Overview 
Moburst Overview:
	Moburst is a full-service, mobile-first marketing agency that helps companies scale and become leaders in their category. Moburst prides itself on solving tough digital challenges for clients, believing that creative thinking, advanced technology, and data-driven insights drive success at scale. 


While Moburst initially focused on providing mobile app marketing services, we soon broadened our horizons, increasing our service roster from 5 to over 28 mobile and digital marketing services, including ASO (app store optimization), influencer marketing & UGC, SEO, media buying, website design & development, and much more. Our transformation was driven by a vision to offer a comprehensive suite of digital services, while keeping the mobile-first experience at the forefront of our efforts, providing clients with an all-in-one solution.


Moburst's daily mission is to innovate creative solutions that connect brands with highly targeted audiences, leading to loyal users. Over 700 brands, from startups to global brands like Google, Discovery, Uber, Samsung, Barnes and Noble, and Reddit, have leveraged the agency’s services to enhance their products and maximize their KPIs.


Please review and become familiar with our website, including the following key pages/sections:
* Home page: https://www.moburst.com/ 
* Blog: https://www.moburst.com/blog/ 
* Services: https://www.moburst.com/digital-marketing-services/ 
* Case Studies (more will be added in the upcoming months): https://www.moburst.com/work/ 
	Target Audience:
	General Target Audience: Business decision-makers, startups, and enterprises looking for mobile and digital marketing solutions.
Ideal Target Audience: Fortune 500 Companies, Established Startups (Past Series A), Early Startups, Medium-Large Businesses, Large Corporations.
	Tone of Voice:
	Professional, knowledgeable, and approachable. Balances industry expertise with a conversational style to engage readers.
	Key Company Phrases:
	* "Become a category leader"
* “Elevate your marketing strategy”
* "Mobile success"
* "Hypergrowth strategies"
* “Experience hypergrowth”
* "Transform your digital presence"
* "Data-driven insights"
* “Measurable performance”
* "Innovative mobile solutions"
	Phrases to Avoid:
	Jargon-heavy terms, overly technical language without explanation, negative connotations, or phrases that may imply uncertainty or lack of expertise.
	Objectives 
	Increase brand awareness, drive traffic to the website, establish Moburst as an authority in mobile & digital marketing, generate leads, and support AEO efforts.
	Funnel Stages (for content):
	* Awareness: Industry trends, introductory guides, and educational content. 
* Consideration: Detailed case studies, comparison articles, and in-depth how-to guides. 
* Conversion, Retention & Upselling: Specific service comparisons, success stories, and ROI-focused content.

	Incorporate relevant infographics, statistics, and videos to encourage engagement and understanding. Do not include any generic images (Shutterstock, or otherwise). Infographics are encouraged and should be indicated in the suggestions.

design_style_synthesis.color_usage: Anchor every composition on a deep near-black ground — dark navy to charcoal — that occupies 60-80% of the total canvas area. Electric cyan and bright blue are the dominant accent lights, used in background rays, glows, and holographic wireframes. The Moburst logo mark injects four distinct colors (cyan-blue, yellow-green, magenta-red, and yellow) as the only true multi-color element; these colors do not migrate into body type or layout elements. Warm gold or amber glints appear sparingly as particle or lens-flare effects. A vivid green or lime is used on pill/badge label backgrounds in select posts to signal a category or keyword. Never use a white or light background.
design_style_synthesis.anti_patterns: Never use a white, light, or gradient background — all compositions must be grounded in a deep dark field. Never apply color to body headline type beyond the single cyan or accent emphasis phrase; do not use rainbow, multi-color, or gradient text treatments. Never place a text card that is fully opaque and flat — the text container must always read as semi-transparent and glassy. Never stretch or recolor the logo mark; the geometric icon is always rendered in its four-color form. Never clutter the text card with more than two typographic levels (headline plus one subhead or attribution line) — do not add bullet lists, icons, or decorative rules inside the card itself.
design_style_synthesis.imagery_style: Use cinematic 3D-rendered or AI-generated photorealistic backgrounds exclusively: deep-space environments, illuminated Earth-from-orbit shots, futuristic holographic interfaces, and neon-lit technological scenes. Backgrounds are predominantly dark, with electric-blue, cyan, or cool-teal light sources emanating from a central focal point (beam, satellite dish, holographic ring). On quote cards, use a real portrait photograph of the speaker, well-lit and professional, placed against the same dark starfield or deep-navy background. Decorative 3D floating objects (translucent gems, crystalline shards, leaf forms) appear in corners as ambient accent elements in some posts — these are secondary and should never compete with the text card.
design_style_synthesis.surface_and_texture: The primary text surface is always a frosted dark card: semi-transparent, near-black with a slight blue or neutral undertone, rendered with soft rounded corners and subtle inner glow or border highlight. The card reads as glassy or glassmorphic — no hard opaque boxes, no flat matte fills. Background imagery carries cinematic depth, atmospheric haze, and volumetric lighting; never flat illustration or clean vector art. Floating ambient props (gems, crystals) carry a 3D rendered, physically-based reflective surface. The overall texture language is premium digital-dark: sleek, dimensional, slightly futuristic.
design_style_synthesis.composition_patterns: Place the logo centered or upper-left within the top 10-15% of the canvas on every post. Use a frosted dark card — rounded rectangle with approximately 12-16px corner radius, semi-transparent dark fill — to contain the primary headline text, positioned in the vertical center of the frame, occupying 40-55% of canvas height. Layer a full-bleed cinematic background image behind the card, with the card floating above it. On carousel covers, reserve the bottom-left corner for a small slide counter (e.g. '01 / 07') at low opacity. On quote and landscape-format posts, split the canvas roughly 50/50 horizontally between a text block on the left and a visual or portrait subject on the right.
design_style_synthesis.platform_adaptations: Instagram feed (square/portrait 4:5): Use the full cinematic background with centered frosted card layout; logo centered top; carousel slide counter bottom-left at low opacity. Instagram Reels: Prioritize the background motion element (animated glow, particle drift) and condense the text card to a single punchy headline line in the center third; logo remains top-center. LinkedIn (landscape 1.91:1): Adopt a left-text / right-visual split composition; logo moves to upper-left; the frosted card becomes a left-anchored vertical panel rather than a centered overlay; portrait photography of a speaker integrates naturally in this format. TikTok: Not evidenced in these references.
design_style_synthesis.typography_treatment: Use a single rounded sans-serif typeface (consistent with Inter, SF Pro, or a close geometric equivalent) across all posts. Headlines run at weight 400-500 for the body of the sentence, with one or two key words set at weight 700-800 to create emphasis — never all-caps headlines. Subheadings and supporting lines run at weight 400, 60-70% of headline size, center-aligned within the card. A distinct bright accent — cyan or a warm highlight — is applied selectively to one phrase per headline in article-cover posts to further direct attention. All text within cards is white on the dark semi-transparent surface; no colored text backgrounds except for pill/badge labels.
design_style_synthesis.mood_and_voice_visual: Authoritative — sharp, declarative headline copy set in high-contrast white type against a dark frosted card, key claim made unmissable by a weight-700 emphasis word, with no decorative flourishes inside the card. Futuristic — every background environment is deep space, orbital, or holographic, communicating technological ambition through cinematic sci-fi visual language rather than flat data charts or photography. Confident-casual — the tone leans editorial (short punchy sentences, rhetorical framing) rather than corporate, reflected in sentence-case headlines and the use of conversational contractions; the layout gives the headline room to breathe with generous padding inside the card.
design_style_synthesis.logo_and_marks_treatment: The Moburst logo — lowercase wordmark 'moburst' in white accompanied by a multi-colored geometric paper-plane/arrow mark to its right — appears on every in-feed post without exception. On portrait/square carousel posts it is centered horizontally in the upper zone, occupying approximately 20-25% of canvas width, placed 5-8% from the top edge. On landscape posts it is placed upper-left at similar scale. The logo mark (the multi-color geometric icon) is always presented in full color; the wordmark is always white. The logo never appears reversed, monochrome, or at reduced opacity. A secondary product wordmark ('Answerburst by moburst') may replace or accompany the main logo on sub-brand posts, following the same top-center placement.

design_style_synthesis.color_usage: Anchor every composition on a deep near-black ground — dark navy to charcoal — that occupies 60-80% of the total canvas area. The Moburst logo mark injects four distinct colors (cyan-blue, yellow-green, magenta-red, and yellow) as the only true multi-color element; these colors do not migrate into body type or layout elements. Warm gold or amber glints appear sparingly as particle or lens-flare effects. A vivid green or lime is used on pill/badge label backgrounds in select posts to signal a category or keyword. Never use a white or light background.
design_style_synthesis.anti_patterns: Never use a white, light, or gradient background — all compositions must be grounded in a deep dark field. Never apply color to body headline type beyond the single cyan or accent emphasis phrase; do not use rainbow, multi-color, or gradient text treatments. Never place a text card that is fully opaque and flat — the text container must always read as semi-transparent and glassy. Never stretch or recolor the logo mark; the geometric icon is always rendered in its four-color form. Never clutter the text card with more than two typographic levels (headline plus one subhead or attribution line) — do not add bullet lists, icons, or decorative rules inside the card itself.
design_style_synthesis.imagery_style: Use cinematic 3D-rendered or AI-generated photorealistic backgrounds exclusively: deep-space environments, illuminated Earth-from-orbit shots, futuristic holographic interfaces, and neon-lit technological scenes. Backgrounds are predominantly dark, with electric-blue, cyan, or cool-teal light sources emanating from a central focal point (beam, satellite dish, holographic ring). On quote cards, use a real portrait photograph of the speaker, well-lit and professional, placed against the same dark starfield or deep-navy background. Decorative 3D floating objects (translucent gems, crystalline shards, leaf forms) appear in corners as ambient accent elements in some posts — these are secondary and should never compete with the text card.
design_style_synthesis.surface_and_texture: The primary text surface is always a frosted dark card: semi-transparent, near-black with a slight blue or neutral undertone, rendered with soft rounded corners and subtle inner glow or border highlight. The card reads as glassy or glassmorphic — no hard opaque boxes, no flat matte fills. Background imagery carries cinematic depth, atmospheric haze, and volumetric lighting; never flat illustration or clean vector art. Floating ambient props (gems, crystals) carry a 3D rendered, physically-based reflective surface. The overall texture language is premium digital-dark: sleek, dimensional, slightly futuristic.
design_style_synthesis.composition_patterns: Place the logo centered or upper-left within the top 10-15% of the canvas on every post. Use a frosted dark card — rounded rectangle with approximately 12-16px corner radius, semi-transparent dark fill — to contain the primary headline text, positioned in the vertical center of the frame, occupying 40-55% of canvas height. Layer a full-bleed cinematic background image behind the card, with the card floating above it. On carousel covers, reserve the bottom-left corner for a small slide counter (e.g. '01 / 07') at low opacity. On quote and landscape-format posts, split the canvas roughly 50/50 horizontally between a text block on the left and a visual or portrait subject on the right.
design_style_synthesis.platform_adaptations: Instagram feed (square/portrait 4:5): Use the full cinematic background with centered frosted card layout; logo centered top; carousel slide counter bottom-left at low opacity. Instagram Reels: Prioritize the background motion element (animated glow, particle drift) and condense the text card to a single punchy headline line in the center third; logo remains top-center. LinkedIn (landscape 1.91:1): Adopt a left-text / right-visual split composition; logo moves to upper-left; the frosted card becomes a left-anchored vertical panel rather than a centered overlay; portrait photography of a speaker integrates naturally in this format. TikTok: Not evidenced in these references.
design_style_synthesis.typography_treatment: Use a single rounded sans-serif typeface (consistent with Inter, SF Pro, or a close geometric equivalent) across all posts. Headlines run at weight 400-500 for the body of the sentence, with one or two key words set at weight 700-800 to create emphasis — never all-caps headlines. Subheadings and supporting lines run at weight 400, 60-70% of headline size, center-aligned within the card. A distinct bright accent — cyan or a warm highlight — is applied selectively to one phrase per headline in article-cover posts to further direct attention. All text within cards is white on the dark semi-transparent surface; no colored text backgrounds except for pill/badge labels.
design_style_synthesis.mood_and_voice_visual: Authoritative — sharp, declarative headline copy set in high-contrast white type against a dark frosted card, key claim made unmissable by a weight-700 emphasis word, with no decorative flourishes inside the card. Futuristic — every background environment is deep space, orbital, or holographic, communicating technological ambition through cinematic sci-fi visual language rather than flat data charts or photography. Confident-casual — the tone leans editorial (short punchy sentences, rhetorical framing) rather than corporate, reflected in sentence-case headlines and the use of conversational contractions; the layout gives the headline room to breathe with generous padding inside the card.
design_style_synthesis.logo_and_marks_treatment: The Moburst logo — lowercase wordmark 'moburst' in white accompanied by a multi-colored geometric paper-plane/arrow mark to its right — appears on every in-feed post without exception. On portrait/square carousel posts it is centered horizontally in the upper zone, occupying approximately 20-25% of canvas width, placed 5-8% from the top edge. On landscape posts it is placed upper-left at similar scale. The logo mark (the multi-color geometric icon) is always presented in full color; the wordmark is always white. The logo never appears reversed, monochrome, or at reduced opacity. A secondary product wordmark ('Answerburst by moburst') may replace or accompany the main logo on sub-brand posts, following the same top-center placement.

top_performing_content: Checklist-style LinkedIn documents won: practical growth frameworks and swipeable explainers earned the strongest click volume.

recommendations: LinkedIn carousel twice weekly: turn one client result or KPI lesson into a proof-led case-study document and track clicks per post.
Instagram carousel weekly: repurpose the best LinkedIn point of view into a swipeable explainer and track engagement rate per post.
Facebook single image weekly: cross-post one LinkedIn insight or proof point and measure non-zero engagement on three of four posts.

platform_breakdown.headline: LinkedIn is the core conversion channel: Clicks remained concentrated here even as reach and video eased month over month.
insights: Click intent stayed strongest here: LinkedIn generated 464 clicks and 521 engagements, making it the clearest lower-funnel platform.
Volume slipped and reach followed: 11 posts this month versus 14 prior coincided with a 29.1% drop in impressions.
Documents led performance: the top checklist post earned 210 clicks, reinforcing carousel-style education over lighter link posts.

platform_breakdown.headline: Instagram is the growth bright spot: Low volume still produced stronger reach and interaction than the prior month.
insights: Efficiency improved with limited output: two posts delivered a 67.7% rise in impressions and a 300% lift in engagements.
Carousel education is the current fit: both top Instagram posts were albums built around AEO and AI-search explainers.
Video is not proven here yet: views fell 73.3%, so keep Instagram focused on carousels before scaling Reels.

platform_breakdown.headline: Facebook needs a steady baseline: One post left the channel too quiet to contribute meaningful engagement.
insights: Activity was minimal: one post produced 625 impressions but only one engagement, so consistency matters more than creative variety first.
Video can still support reach: the platform logged 90 video views, suggesting lightweight repurposed clips are viable.
Competitive pressure is volume-led: SplitMetrics posted regularly on Facebook, while Moburst posted once and lost continuity.

competitive_takeaways: Cadence gap needs immediate action: Moburst posts 3.3 times weekly versus the 4.5 competitor average.
Share of voice can grow through consistency: 19% supports adding Instagram and Facebook without weakening LinkedIn.
LinkedIn should keep leading: Gummicube and SplitMetrics both sustain heavier posting around repeatable expert narratives.
Facebook requires baseline coverage: SplitMetrics posted 12 times there while Moburst posted once in the period.

sprout_performance_analysis.month_over_month_summary: Video softness was the biggest move: views fell 49.2%, pulling down overall engagement even as click intent stayed comparatively resilient. Instagram was the exception, with stronger reach and interaction, while LinkedIn remained the primary demand channel.
key_insights: LinkedIn still carries demand generation: It drove 464 of 465 clicks, so recovery starts with stronger document and thought-leadership volume there.
Cadence trails the category: Moburst posted 3.3 times per week versus a 4.5 competitor average, limiting share of voice and repeat exposure.
Channel mix is the clearest gap: 11 of 14 tracked posts were on LinkedIn, while Instagram and Facebook remained too light to build consistency.
Engagement quality is uneven by network: Instagram improved sharply month over month, but Facebook activity stayed near zero and needs a weekly baseline.
Thought leadership beats promotion: Posts framed as strategic questions, checklists, and AI-search explainers outperformed broader brand or link-out messaging.
top_performing_content: Checklist-style LinkedIn documents won: practical growth frameworks and swipeable explainers earned the strongest click volume.
Provocative AI-search hooks worked: contrast-led openings on AEO, agents, and recommendations drove attention across LinkedIn and Instagram.
Expert-led educational content landed: posts featuring internal leaders and clear strategic takes consistently ranked among top performers.

recommendations: LinkedIn carousel twice weekly: turn one client result or KPI lesson into a proof-led case-study document and track clicks per post.
Instagram carousel weekly: repurpose the best LinkedIn point of view into a swipeable explainer and track engagement rate per post.
Facebook single image weekly: cross-post one LinkedIn insight or proof point and measure non-zero engagement on three of four posts.

platform_breakdown.headline: LinkedIn is the core conversion channel: Clicks remained concentrated here even as reach and video eased month over month.
insights: Click intent stayed strongest here: LinkedIn generated 464 clicks and 521 engagements, making it the clearest lower-funnel platform.
Volume slipped and reach followed: 11 posts this month versus 14 prior coincided with a 29.1% drop in impressions.
Documents led performance: the top checklist post earned 210 clicks, reinforcing carousel-style education over lighter link posts.

platform_breakdown.headline: Instagram is the growth bright spot: Low volume still produced stronger reach and interaction than the prior month.
insights: Efficiency improved with limited output: two posts delivered a 67.7% rise in impressions and a 300% lift in engagements.
Carousel education is the current fit: both top Instagram posts were albums built around AEO and AI-search explainers.
Video is not proven here yet: views fell 73.3%, so keep Instagram focused on carousels before scaling Reels.

platform_breakdown.headline: Facebook needs a steady baseline: One post left the channel too quiet to contribute meaningful engagement.
insights: Activity was minimal: one post produced 625 impressions but only one engagement, so consistency matters more than creative variety first.
Video can still support reach: the platform logged 90 video views, suggesting lightweight repurposed clips are viable.
Competitive pressure is volume-led: SplitMetrics posted regularly on Facebook, while Moburst posted once and lost continuity.

competitive_takeaways: Cadence gap needs immediate action: Moburst posts 3.3 times weekly versus the 4.5 competitor average.
Share of voice can grow through consistency: 19% supports adding Instagram and Facebook without weakening LinkedIn.
LinkedIn should keep leading: Gummicube and SplitMetrics both sustain heavier posting around repeatable expert narratives.
Facebook requires baseline coverage: SplitMetrics posted 12 times there while Moburst posted once in the period.
